I said at the beginning 500 reckoning with the distance between the football pitch and the tavern, and I -- and I reckoned that it could be those streets of 20 metres each plus the football pitch. That's why I said 250. My house overlooked the pitch. There was the church, then my house, and the pitch that my house was facing. But if the pitch is not 500 metres, then it could be less.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I would like you to take a look at a document quickly before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It is Exhibit P130 at tab 20. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document you probably have not seen before. It is information --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Could you make it a bit larger?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. On the top left-hand corner, you see Command of the 1st Military District, and it is dated October of 1991. And the title is: "The conduct of the Commander of the Special Forces of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem ... 'Arkan' in Erdut." This is a military report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I would like us to go to page 3 in the English version and page 2 in the B/C/S version. And we can zoom on the bottom part of the B/C/S version. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are flipping through the pages too quickly. I didn't manage to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I want you to focus on this part of the report because the other parts of the report are of no concern to us at this moment. It talks about Arkan and his activities. And it says: "In the centre" -- And I'd like to remind you this document is drafted from October of 1991. "... Arkan is engaged in the slaughter of the prisoners sent by the local territorial units. He observed a man being beaten with a baseball bat, after which they put him on the nylon to bleed to death. "He observed them putting rifles with silencers against the back of the head of four men and killing them in that way. Following the slaughter of these four men, who were then thrown in the Dunav River, he personally wiped off the blood." Sir, were there any rumours at that time about prisoners being thrown in the Danube river?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Not that I know. I am not aware of this. Maybe the person who did this was aware of it, and I don't suppose they would talk about it. This is the first time I hear of it. I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, your building was in the same compound as Arkan's training centre. Here we have a military report from the 1st Military District whose headquarters are quite removed from Erdut, and you're telling us that you have never heard of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that these two objects were in the same compound, and I don't see any foundation for such a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I could refrain or rephrase the question, I see it's the break, though. So before we go on break, however, Your Honours, I did fail to tender the document I showed earlier with respect to Mr. Ulemek. This was 65 ter 6534, tab 14. We wish to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would object because the witness didn't know anything about this document and it is not -- there is no foundation for tendering this document through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the witness is familiar with the individual who is referred to in the document. He is familiar with the ID card that he personally possessed. We are submitting it to ascertain the fact that there is a match between these IDs and that this person did, in fact, have an ID card as described in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, the purpose of this document is not, as far as I know, whether the witness know Mr. Ulemek or not, but the match between these IDs. We did not see Ulemek's ID, and we don't know about authenticity and credibility of this card mentioned in this report. Because of that, I think that there is no foundation to tender this document through this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you wanted to intervene? Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did want to intervene. As far as I was able to read from that official ID card, I had not seen that ID card as I did mine, but it is -- it has the same writing, the same text as my ID card, but I didn't see it. I didn't see his actual ID with his photo on it. He could have written it himself. I saw that kind of ID several times, and now I find out that he had the same kind, Ulemek. He didn't have our ID card. He had the ID card of Arkan's unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The objection is overruled. The document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Does 65 ter number 6534 need to be under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It is meant to be under seal. Thank you for reminder.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3263, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I believe it is the appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. There is one little detail I wanted to mention. On the document we MFI'd which was the witness statement of this witness, right, Mr. Demirdjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I suppose then there were another -- I suppose it's a confusion, but another issue will be resolved; namely, that the witness statement says that the witness has been interviewed by Mr. Zoran Zivanovic and by -- and then there is the witness's name. I don't suppose he is interviewed by himself. Just -- I want to have that on the record. Mr. Witness, we take the second break. We'll come back at 12.45. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I think this morning I forgot to mention for the record, so do I it now, that today we sit pursuant to Rule 15 bis; Judge Mindua being absent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And, Your Honours, as promised before the break, I did look back at the transcript at the portion which was in private session. I believe that as of page 46, line 2, we can assume that this is back in private session [sic] as nothing was said about the document any further from that point on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So I called the document at page 42, line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So from that -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You say: "As of page 46, line 2, we can assume that this is back in private ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In open.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Open.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's totally different. The private -- we lift the qualification private session as from that point. Please proceed, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Dafinic, I would like to ask you about the statement that you gave to the Defence. Could you tell us first what was the very first time that you got in contact or communicated with Mr. Hadzic or any members of his Defence team about testifying in this case?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: I did not have contact with Mr. Hadzic. I had contact on the 29th of May, 2014 with Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the very first time, not the very last time. So the 29th of May you signed this statement. But what was the first time that you communicated with the Defence team of Mr. Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes, well, it was in April. Perhaps one month before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So that was the very, very first time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: In the month of April, the first time and the last time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, the first time time was in April. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us where -- were you met in Novi Sad where you live?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And both in April and in May you met the Defence team in Novi Sad?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: I met with Zoran in April; and in May; I met with Aleksandar from his team to sign the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to take you first to the meeting in April. Where exactly in Novi Sad did this take place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: In the centre of Novi Sad. In the offices of Mico Crnogorac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This is a lawyer, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No, it's not law firm. It's a friend's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, you said that Mr. Zivanovic was present during the interview. Was anyone else present while -- during this interview?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And tell us who else was there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: He and I conducted the interview together, and David Cesic, I think, was present. I don't know. As soon as I finished the interview with him, I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: How long did the interview last?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: An hour and a half, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And when you met again in May to sign the statement, was it in the same office?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And was Mr. David Cesic present as well when you signed the statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes. I got the statement to read and to sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And both in April and May when you met in this office, was Mr. Cesic part of the discussions during the interview?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Was he present in the office?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: In another office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now this morning we saw the ID card which had gone missing. You mention this at paragraph 21. And I would like to take you to paragraph 21 of your signed statement. Do you have it in front of you? You see here at paragraph 21 you say that: "After the formation of the RSK, we received new identity cards from Ilija Kojic, but for some reason, I do not know why, we had to return them after a month, which is why I do not have this identity card." So I'm curious to know, how did you find it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Well, I photocopied all the documents I received. From day one, I made photocopies in order not to lose them and also to keep them as a memento. In case they had to returned or were taken away, I wanted to have photocopies. So I found, quite by chance, this photocopy among my documents in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to move to another topic. You mentioned Vukasin Soskocanin at paragraph 3 of your statement, and you mention that he organised the guards in Borovo Selo after Hadzic's arrest and Savic's arrest in Plitvice. Now, at this paragraph here you add that: "At this time Vukasin Soskocanin was not a member of the SDS but he joined later." Right? The last sentence of paragraph 3, this is what you say. He was not a member of the SDS. He joined later. Now, sir, we know that Mr. Hadzic and Mr. Savic were arrested on the 31st of March, 1991, and we know that Vukasin Soskocanin was killed on the 15th of May, 1991, so six weeks later. So how and when during this six-weeks period did he join the SDS, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Well, I think he joined the SDS even later than that. Not within those six weeks. Later than that. I don't know the exact date. He was imagining a different kind of movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we pull up the Exhibit P65.50, Your Honours. It's at tab 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And while this is coming up, Mr. Dafinic, I'm not sure I quite understand your answer. I'm telling you that six weeks after Mr. Hadzic's arrest, Vukasin Soskocanin was killed on the 15th of May, and you're saying he was -- he joined the SDS even later than that? I'm not sure I understand exactly your answer.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Here it is. When Goran Hadzic and Boro Savic were released at Plitvice Lakes, they came to see Soskocanin. They came for a meeting which I also attended, although I didn't come in to listen to what they're talking about. But he was not a member of the SDS then. As far as I know, he joined later. Maybe he had joined earlier, but not that I know. To the best of my knowledge he joined the SDS, became a member, later. Maybe he had joined earlier without telling me, but the fact that he was meeting with Goran Hadzic and Savic does not necessarily mean he was a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's Exhibit P62.50. I see that it was recorded as P675.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stevo Bogic got him to sign up to the SDS. Stevo Bogic could know the date, when Soskocanin joined the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise. It's P65.50.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Dafinic. The document will come up in a moment. This is not the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see the document on your screen? It is dated the 12th of November, 1990. And this is a list of members of the SDS in Borovo. And you can see as number 1 Vukasin Soskocanin as president of the SDS there. Is this something -- does this help you establish the time-line a little bit or --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: I can see that, yes. It does help. That means he was a member earlier without me knowing. Yes, yes. It helps me. I see that it's the 12th of November, 1990, but I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, when you met with the members of the Defence team here in the last couple of days, they made some notes about what you said about Vukasin Soskocanin. And one thing which was not put to you this morning, and I would like you to confirm that this is something you said in proofing, was that after the Borovo Selo incident, Soskocanin stated for the media that he personally killed five Ustashas during the battle in Borovo Selo on the 2nd of May, 1991. Is that accurate, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: It's accurate. He made that statement for TV Novi Sad. That's what he said and there must be some recording kept at Television Novi Sad. I saw it on TV in the first place. He was shown on television saying, "I killed five them in battle and I will kill 55 more," in combat, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, if someone is claiming on TV that he killed five person on -- in a battle and he would kill 55 [as interpreted] more, would you agree that this is quite an extreme position?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The other number was "505," not "55."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, I want us to move to the issue of the attack on Dalj which you talked about this morning. You mentioned that you were in a group led by Marko Loncarevic. Can you tell us how large this group was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Which item? Which point?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It doesn't matter at this moment, but could you remember independently from the statement how many people were there in this group led by Marko Loncarevic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Five or six.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now you also say that you found out about the attack no more than half an hour prior to the departure. This is something you said paragraph 14 of your statement. Do you stand by that statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now you found out no more than half an hour prior to the departure.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Were you, however, aware that an attack was imminent and that there were some plans in the workings?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No. He told me to come to the hall, and when I arrived, there were already about a hundred people there. I didn't even know that there would be an attack. He just told me to come to the hall and there was some attack being planned. He told me that in the hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, was there any arming happening prior to the attack in preparation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Well, everybody was armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Specifically -- I'm talking about specifically for the attack. Was there any arming being conducted a day or two days earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Well, everybody had weapons even before. We were told to come with our weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Can we display 65 ter 6639 at tab 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm going to show awe document in a moment, Mr. Dafinic. This is an Official Note. And just to give you context, it's given by a man by the name of Zdenko Nenic; he lives in Borovo. Are you familiar with this name?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You've never heard of a man named Zdenko Nenic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we could move to page 3 in the B/C/S first --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please enlarge the text?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, just a moment. I will ask them to enlarge the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So this is page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's a very long statement, Mr. Dafinic. I will show you the relevant portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Page 3 in B/C/S is equivalent to page 2 in the English version. And I'd like to -- for the B/C/S version, if we could scroll -- yeah, zoom on the bottom part, please, in the last three paragraphs. Yes, exactly. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this man Nenic says here that in June or July 1991 Marko Loncarevic, which is somebody we've spoken about earlier today, approached him to take over some weapons which he would take to his own house. And in the next paragraph, Mr. Nenic says that he agreed to take over the weapons, and following a prior agreement with Loncarevic he went to Jovica Vucenovic's house where they took over at least four wooden military boxes. Now, it is correct to say that Mr. Vucenovic was in the TO in Borovo Selo; is that right, Mr. Dafinic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, if we go to the next page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Here it says that, in the top part: "After they had cleaned the weapons, Loncarevic instructed them to take the weapons to the Orthodox church in Borovo and store them in Milenko Dafinic's house which stood in the immediate vicinity of the church. The interviewee remembers that when they arrived at that location, they did not find Dafinic."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page in the English version and also in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So they did not find Dafinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we move to the top part of the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: "... at home, his wife, Jovanka, nee Blagojevic, and Milenko's father showed them where to put the weapons. Talking to Dafinic several days later, the interviewee learned that the weapons were destined for Dalj because an attack on that village was being planned." Now, sir, does that remind you a little bit of the arming that was taking place at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it does refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And it carries on here to talk about a -- one or two nights ago a meeting which was led by Marko Loncarevic and where several people were gathered in a hall. Does that also match with your recollection of the events?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the first part. My wife wasn't there at the time, and my father doesn't live in the same house as me so he could not have been there. So this is not clear to me. My wife was absent as a displaced person, and my father lives at a different address in a street called Skolska. So this is entirely unclear to me. As to weapons, yes, there were weapons. But as to my wife and my father being there, that's impossible. My father knew absolutely nothing about what I was doing, and the same goes for my wife. Especially since she wasn't there even.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: But do you agree that you did know a couple of days earlier that the attack was being planned? Do you agree on that part of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: I agree that the weapons were cleaned and left in my place and in Jovica Vucenovic's place, but I do not agree as to knowing about when the attack was going to be carried out. I did not know it several days in advance, and I would not have taken the risk of having the weapons cleaned in my house. I would not have exposed my family to such a risk.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I tender this statement, which was at tab 17, 65 ter number is 6639.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would object, because this statement does not fulfil the requirements from Rule 92 ter, bis, or quater to be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, it's strictly for impeachment purposes, Your Honours, and not for the substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The relevant parts are already read and there is no need to tender this document for the impeachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Objection sustained. We will not admit the document. Everything is on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Much obliged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Dafinic, I would like to return to the issue of your group, the government security group. You mention in your statement that Mr. Zarko Aleksic was involved in theft, and you seem to have focused mainly on his activities in your statement as far as members of your group are concerned. Is there any reason why you spoke about Aleksic's involvement and not the other members of your group?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: There is no special reason except I never learned anything about others. I simply didn't learn about others. And as for Aleksic, the facts were there. It's not that I focused on him. I simply told you everything I knew and what I had heard. I didn't see it. I heard that about Stevo Bogic. I didn't catch him stealing. I simply heard that he had done it. I didn't focus on him. I simply told you what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In terms of catching him stealing, was Mr. Aleksic ever set up? Was there a trap set for him to see if he was stealing?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not the one to tell you about that. Perhaps he was set up. I simply don't know. I didn't. I'm not the right person to answer that question. I didn't set him up. And as for others, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, with respect to others, isn't it true, sir, that Sinisa Gajic and Dragan Lazarevic were involved in stealing money from a bakery in Dalj just following the take-over on the 1st of August of 1991? Is that something you were familiar with at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. They were not in my group, not during the assault. I didn't know anything about that. Really nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you find out about it afterwards at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No. I sold Sinisa Gajic a small Ferguson tractor and some tools. I did not have anything to live on, so he [as interpreted] sold a tractor, a trailer. He gave me a certain amount of money which -- with which I bought food for my family who were in exile. I can't even -- I could not even dream that he would be participating in the thing that you're describing. I thought he had money. By then, I had all dispensed all of my money. In order to be able to survive, I had to start selling my belongings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just one correction in the transcript or in interpretation. It is line 14. It is said: "I did not have anything to live on, so he sold the tractor ..." The witness said "I sold ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: "... the tractor."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with a restaurant in Erdut Planina which at the time was called Saran?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No, I did not go there before the war or during the war. I never went there. I moved in the direction of Vukovar and Borovo Naselje. Those were our locations. Perhaps I went to Trpinja and Bogota, but the places you mention in your question, no, I never went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: No, you never went there but had you heard of it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you know that there was a restaurant in Erdut Planina which was owned by a Hungarian man who was known as Ferika, last name Pap.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No, I never went to that side. I went to Okonja's bar. A good bar. There were six pubs or bars in Borovo Selo, so I did not have any reason to go elsewhere. I didn't even go to Dalj. I went to a totally different side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the time that you were in Borovo Selo. I'm talking about the time where you stayed, as you said earlier, in the government building in Erdut. Now, Erdut Planina is not very far from Erdut, is it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now during your time there, have you not ever heard about this restaurant and his owner? So I'm talking about September 1991 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything because I didn't go there. I didn't have time. I had a lot of commitments. I didn't hear. I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, we have information that Mr. Pap was brought for interrogation at Arkan's training centre in November of 1991. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Did you know a man by the name of Milorad Stricevic, who was also known as Puki?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: I used to see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you know that as part of his work he -- it was charged [sic] of interrogating prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No, no. No. He didn't brag about that. And why would he ever tell me that? I keep on repeating that I was a guard, and if he was a colonel and if I was a guard, why would he ever confide in me? Of course no, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Stricevic interrogated the owner of this restaurant, Mr. Pap, in the training centre, and there are suggestions that you are present during this interrogation and took part in the mistreatment of this restaurant owner.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: First of all, as I've already told you, I did pass by the centre. And as a foot soldier, as a regular soldier, I did not have access to the centre, so I never entered it. The discipline over there was such that nobody could enter if they were not authorised.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: But if they were invited --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Really nobody. Nobody. What? What? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: But if they were invited to attend, they could, couldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: If somebody was to invite me?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, let's move on a bit here because it is also suggested that Mr. Pap's --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- Mr. Pap's wife was looking for him, and this became a bit of a disturbance in Erdut because she kept asking about him. Were you familiar with the fact that a woman was looking for her disappeared husband? And we're talking about the period of November 1991.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, she never approached me when I was on sentry duty. She never came to our facility. I don't know about the others, but she never approached me with that request.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Didn't Stevo Bogic order you, Sinisa Gajic, and Zarko Aleksic to go to her house, confiscate money from this woman, and arrest her?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No. I've never heard such thing. First of all, he was not in a position to give me such an order. He could not order me to do such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Wasn't he your superior?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes. But in terms of securing the government, he was not there to tell me to arrest people, because he knew I would never do that. I'm sure he knew that very well. Well, I mean, why don't you ask him? I'm sure he will tell you that he knows that I would never do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If you are ordered to arrest someone and you have a pass which allows you to arrest someone, why are you telling us that you would never arrest someone?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Why wouldn't I arrest people? And in the ID it said that we were authorised to bring people in, that we could do that. But there were no grounds. I did not have any grounds to do that. I'm not a police officer. I'm not an investigative body. I was not trained to interrogate people. It was the police that did that. We were provided with official ID cards to move about freely, not to arrest and bring in people. I was not qualified for such things. Professionals, qualified people, trained police officers are -- were supposed to do that and not me. And I would have never done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with a woman who was a cook in the government building's kitchen by the name of Viktorija Albert?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: There were several cooks but none of their names ring any bells.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this particular cook was in a friendly relation with Mr. Milorad Stricevic. Did you ever hear that Arkan dismissed Stricevic from his position for protecting Ms. Albert and her family?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. That was beyond my rank and beyond my sphere of interest. I never heard that. I keep on repeating: Why would anybody be discussing things like that in front of me? Again, I don't understand what you're saying. Why would Arkan ever say that to me or whoever? No, I never heard any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I did not suggest that he would have told you, personally. What I'm saying here is that it was well known that Mr. Stricevic was protecting this family and that he was dismissed and that effectively we know that he was also killed. Do you know about the circumstances of his death?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No. When it comes to Arkan's personnel policy, I was not in a position to know whom he promoted, whom he removed. There were lot of people there that belonged to him, but I did not have a clue of what was going on, and none of them ever told anything to us. I suppose that they did not dare say anything to us. So how would I have obtained such information? Sometime when they passed by us, they would say, "Hello." Sometimes not even that. They just frowned upon us. That was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, were you familiar with the fact that Ms. Albert's home, which was very close to the government building, was appropriated and turned into a brothel? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the fact that there was a brothel in Erdut very close to the government building?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: I heard about that, but it was kept secret from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You never went there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we display 65 ter 6638, please. Tab 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, what we're looking at here is the statement of a woman named Katica Dagovic who lives in Borovo.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: What's the name? Katica what? Dagovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Quite right. Did you know her?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: She seems to be familiar with you. And I would like you to look at -- first of all, at page 1, we see her name.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I did know her, but I can't remember her. She doesn't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, she was born on the 21st of June, 1960, so at the time of the events, she was around 21, 22 years old. And what she describes here is the events in Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And I'd like us to go to page 3 in both the English and the B/C/S version. In the B/C/S version, we can zoom on the -- well, if you're in the English version, zoom on the bottom part. Thank you. Now top part in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Here she describes about individuals who carried out especially brutal persecution of Croatian population in Borovo Selo itself. She lists a number of people, including Stevo Bogic, Branko Ciric, you're listed there, so is Mr. David Cesic, and other members of your group.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now if we move to page 4 in the English version. The bottom part of page 4. The very last paragraph. And the B/C/S version, we scroll down a little bit. In fact, we'll need to go to the next page in the B/C/S version. Top part. Yeah. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The paragraph begins with: "During 1993 ..." She explains that her husband was mobilised in the JNA, so she was alone in her house with her two daughters. "At an unspecified date at around 9.30 at night, someone rang at the house doorbell. Milenko Dafinic stood in the doorway dressed in civilian clothes and told her that he needed to talk to her." She describes the conversation you had and that you took her in silence to Erdut to the barracks of Arkan. At the time she was worried about her children. And when you arrived to the building in question, she could see that this was a large facility with a lot of rooms. Next to it there was a coffee bar and a disco which were built up for Arkan's Tigers. There was also a brothel. And she got scared. She describes the brothel here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, do we have all this on the document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I'm still at -- in the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the very last sentence of the paragraph talks about the location of the brothel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We just change the page. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours. Yes, we have to turn the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So this was all in the first paragraph, everything that I described, about being taken to Erdut, to Arkan's barracks, and that she was taken to this brothel, and she got scared. Now, the next paragraph gives some details about the brothel. And in the middle of the paragraph it says that, first of all: "In addition to Arkan, the following men also owned these girls. David Cesic, Stevo Bogic, Milenko Dafinic, Petar Rakas, and Rujo from Savulje who were in league with Hadzic." And in the next paragraph, she says the following: "After arriving at the building, Milenko Dafinic takes the said Katica through to his room and tells her to relax and calm down and that in the end she would even be laughing and that if she won't that she would end her career in an Erdut well." The paragraph carries on to describe that Petar Rakas came in and asked you to return her home and that you returned her home and you apologised on the way. Does this statement refresh your memory about, first of all, this woman and that the fact that you arrested her and brought her over to the location she describes?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: I don't know. First of all, the Russian who's mentioned here, he was not in my group. I never socialised with him. I socialised with Pero Rakas. Why would I take her there? Why would I apologise to her? That woman's name really doesn't ring a bell. Why would I take her there and then return her home? I don't understand why. To show her the brothel. Why would I have done that? This is completely untrue. I know nothing about that. This -- I've never heard of that before or seen it before. That guy, Rujo, and it says Ceca Valiskovic [phoen] was also brought there. I don't know. This is -- I really don't understand. This is totally beyond any common sense. I never participated in this. I'm just reading what I see in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let me stop you for a minute here. The paragraph that you have in front of your eyes right now names Mr. David Cesic, Stevo Bogic, Petar Rakas. Now these are individuals who are part of your group; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But Rujo is not from Savulje. And he says Rujo and Hadzic are in cahoots. What cahoots? He was from in our group, but I didn't do that, and I don't believe that any of them did. But you have to ask them. I'm sure I didn't. I can speak for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So you still stand by your statement that you never arrested anyone and brought them over?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. And particularly not to Arkan's place. I told you, there was no way I could enter Arkan's premises, and I didn't. And Petar Rakas also, Rus [as interpreted], David Cesic. Stevo Bogic, yes, perhaps. But the rest of us, we could not enter those premises at all. There was no way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with the men from Borovo, his name is Dusan Vukovic, he was the son of Father Prako?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Excuse me? Branko? Did you say Branko?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The man's name is Dusan Vukovic, and he is the son of a man who's name is Father Prako, P-r-a-k-o.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Can you jog my memory? It was 20 years ago. I have forgotten some people. Vukovic. Hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This is a man who worked on a raft connecting Borovo Selo to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes, now it does ring a bell. Dusan -- I apologise. What name did you say? What -- what did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Vukovic. Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: If we have the same person in mind, then I know him. He was the one who was in charge of the barge on the Danube. He transported people across the river; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Correct. Now if we look at a statement that he's given.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This is 65 ter 6637 at tab 15. If we zoom in on the first page in the central part -- well, in the first paragraph to start with. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You can see his details here. His name, his date of birth, that he resides in Borovo. In the second paragraph, he states that he was mobilised into the civilian protection and that his superior was Ruza Mandic. And in 1991, he served as an assistant worker on a raft connecting Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, if we turn to page 2 in the English version and in the B/C/S version. The bottom part. Yes. And top part in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic says that he was aware that Branko Ciric, aka Kotsgar [phoen], was the commander of the upper part of the village, and this is Borovo Selo. And he mentions a number of people in his group. And then he mentions a number of people in Goran Hadzic's group, including Relja, Milenko Dafinic, David Cesic, Petar Rakas, Marinac Aleksic, Stevo Bogic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The next paragraph -- if we could go to the next page, please. Top part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It says that Mihajlo Ulemek, the man we mentioned earlier today from Pazova, "committed various crimes in Daljska Planina and that Dafinic has bragged about Ulemek killing people. He also bragged about the systemic rape and orgies taking place at the winery and that Pero Rakas operated a brothel." Now, sir, it appears that this man has a lot of details about your group, and it appears that your group was deeply involved in criminal difficulties, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: That's not true. I don't know why that person stated that. That person and I were on very friendly terms. I saw him actually at Branko Ciric's funeral in Sombor. I would never brag about Ulemek committing crimes. He was my neighbour. He was in charge of the ferry. I don't know why he said that. Maybe he was put under pressure. Maybe he wanted to protect himself or somebody dictated this to him. I don't believe that these are his words. Actually, they are. But I don't believe that he would have said this. First of all, even if I'd known things, I would have not bragged about them. I'm not that kind of a man. But I don't think that this is his statement. I absolutely cannot believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You cannot believe it, sir, but we just saw two people mentioning your group being involved in criminal activities and the creation of this brothel, and what I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I apologise. I don't know who served in that. And how come they knew all that if they were in Borovo Selo? No, no. I don't agree with this. No. No way. I can't believe that he stated this, or perhaps he did but under duress.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you said this morning that you left the region in July of 1997 during the peaceful reintegration.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Up to that point you were living in Erdut; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No, I lived in Borovo Selo. I did live in Erdut until 1993 or, rather, from 1991 to 1993, but I visited my own home very often. Every now and then I would come home. But we spent a lot of nights there as well and then we would go home and stay there for a couple of days and then we would return.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, sir, you mentioned you left in July 1997. Mr. Slavko Dokmanovic was arrested on the 27th of June, 1997. Now isn't it correct that this was -- the news of his arrest were publicly known and were all over the news?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, sir, did you leave the region out of fear that you, too, would be arrested?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: I left like everybody else. A majority of the people left, so I did too. I did not want to go on living there. Not because I was afraid that I would be arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Stevo Bogic also left the region around the same time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: He left earlier. I stayed the longest of all those people. They had to leave earlier because their children started school. At that time my children were already out of school, so there was no reason for me to leave as early as they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And were you familiar with the fact that before you left Mr. Bogic burnt a number of documents relating to the activities of your group right in front of his house in a metal barrel?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No. No, no, no. Neither did he do that in front of my house, nor do I know that. Why would he do that in front of my house in the centre of the village for everyone to see? No, he didn't. If he did that, it must have been farther away. He did not do it in front of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The translation may have been missed in this one. I said that he did it in front of his house. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I thought you suggested he did it in front of my house. They live a lot farther away from me, but I didn't hear about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this concludes my cross-examination. May I offer to tender the two statements we just saw, 65 ter 6637 and 6638. Again, specifically for the purposes of impeachment. Now, I know that some portions of it were read into the record. However, we believe that it would serve the purposes of the Trial Chamber to have these two statements which involve the witness directly into the activities described in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would object, Your Honour. [Microphone not activated] If it is only for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would object if it was for impeachment because it was already in the transcript, and I don't see any need to tender these documents into evidence. There is no foundation for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I be permitted to put one more thing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In terms of the foundation, I believe that we have seen from these two statements that the witnesses are describing the group that the witness has described and which he agrees are members of his group, so I believe that's, from a foundational point of view, we have something really solid in terms of how this is connected to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In that case, it is not for the impeachment purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: No, it's for the foundation. That's the foundation, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We'll come back to this issue later on. Mr. Zivanovic, do you have anything in redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. May we see, please, Exhibit 6639. It is tab 17. Could you zoom in, please. Just first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dafinic, you can see here the name of the police officer who wrote this statement. Do you know that officer? I see his name is Tomislav Farkas.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO DAFINIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know Tomislav Farkas personally, but he once came to see my mother-in-law in Borovo Selo, my daughter -- my wife's house as well, and of course that's my house as well, inherited. And he said that my wife should come to an interview related to some purported murder that I committed and threw the bodies in a well. That was a well that I shared with neighbours, including Pap, before the water-supply, the city water-supply approached Borovo Selo. I first closed it and poured cement over it. And then later we were building a swimming pool and then I activated it again. Anyway, the police officer threatened my wife that they would be taken into custody, both she and her mother, unless she comes for that interview. She was scared and then she told me that -- in fact, she wrote to me asking if she could live with me. I said yes. After that I received information that my mother-in-law, Ruza Blagojevic, was supposed to come to Borovo Selo because a buyer for her house had been found. It was to be sold to Zarko Aleksic, nicknamed The Marine. In fact, the buyer was Zarko Aleksic's brother, and since Zarko Aleksic had bought a house next door, it would be a good idea for me to sell him or, rather, sell his brother that house. That's what I was told. I told him to come so we can make a deal. I would also sell him that house, but I wanted to see him face to face because I don't believe that he would make that statement if he had to look me in the eye.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long has it been since those threats made by Farkas to your mother-in-law, and how long was it between that threat and the offer to sell your house to this Aleksic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this does -- sorry. This does not raise from the cross-examination. The purpose of showing this statement had nothing to do with the man who took this statement. Counsel is now exploring a completely different topic which has nothing to do with the statement, so this does not arise out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is closely related to the document and about Mr. Farkas and his connections with somebody else who is very irrelevant for -- in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And that's exactly the point. It has nothing to do with what I raised in cross-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The document was raised and tried to be tendered, and the portion of these documents were also seated into the transcript without the name of the police officer who took this statement that was challenged by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Rules --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it is very important to assess this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, a document can contain a lot of information. The rules of re-examination is that counsel is limited to the topics which were raised in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would just say that it is weight -- it is go to the weight of the credibility of the document, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I just make a brief remark on this point, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm about to sustain the objection, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very well. I'll save it for next time, because I think there will be a next time in respect of redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please move on, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I've finished my redirect, sorry -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Dafinic, this brings your testimony to an end. We thank you very much for coming to The Hague to assist the Tribunal. You're now released as a witness, and we wish you a safe journey home. The court usher will escort you out of the courtroom. Thank you. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to thank all of you for giving me a chance to tell the truth, and I hope that truth will prevail. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You may leave the courtroom, Mr. Dafinic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: There is one little issue left. On the record, page 55, line 23, where it is written that I said: "We give the qualification private session as from that point," and what I said was: "We will lift the qualification of private session as from that point."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we complete for the day, did you want to hear more about the two statements that we proposed, or is it something that you were planning to deliberate on at a further stage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We are planning to think it over, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned for the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of September, 2014, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.00 p.m.,
